Run continues automatic running, or lets an existing jump continue.

Duck crouches on the ground, or rapidly descends in the air.

Contact ends the game. A jump rises, reaches its peak, falls, and ends; it cannot be extended by repeatedly selecting jump. Duck does not stop horizontal motion.

run: Release duck. Running is automatic; an existing jump continues.
jump: Release duck and start a jump if grounded. No second jump while airborne.
duck: Crouch if grounded; start a rapid descent if airborne.

action.instructions: Which action should the dinosaur take now to survive?

criteria.run: run: Release duck. Running is automatic; an existing jump continues. Example: on the ground with a cactus 500 pixels away, run because it is too far away to jump yet. Example: already airborne above a cactus, let the jump continue.
criteria.jump: jump: Release duck and start a jump if grounded. No second jump while airborne. Example: on the ground with a cactus 60 pixels away, jump to clear the cactus. This action raises the dinosaur over a nearby ground obstacle.
criteria.duck: duck: Crouch if grounded; start a rapid descent if airborne. Example: on the ground with a low flying bird approaching, crouch underneath the bird. This is for overhead obstacles, not cacti on the ground.

exact_action_inputs: run: Release duck. Running is automatic; an existing jump continues. Example: on the ground with a cactus 500 pixels away, run because it is too far away to jump yet. Example: already airborne above a cactus, let the jump continue.

jump: Release duck and start a jump if grounded. No second jump while airborne. Example: on the ground with a cactus 60 pixels away, jump to clear the cactus. This action raises the dinosaur over a nearby ground obstacle.

duck: Crouch if grounded; start a rapid descent if airborne. Example: on the ground with a low flying bird approaching, crouch underneath the bird. This is for overhead obstacles, not cacti on the ground.

Side view of the gap, each dash is approximately 10 pixels: dinosaur |--------------------------------------------------| obstacle.

Example state: The dinosaur is on the ground. A cactus is 180 pixels beyond its front, 25 pixels wide and 50 pixels tall, approaching at 6 pixels per frame. Answer: run. Explanation: Wait for this six-frame turn. Jumping now would put the descent too early, while the cactus is still passing.

Duck crouches on the ground or accelerates descent in the air. Cacti are ground obstacles; birds may leave room underneath. The game pauses while the model decides. The examples below describe other situations. Choose for the current observation at the end, using the examples to understand timing.

Example state: The dinosaur is on the ground. A cactus is 60 pixels beyond its front, 25 pixels wide and 50 pixels tall, moving toward it at 6 pixels per frame. Answer: jump. Explanation: Start rising to clear the approaching cactus; staying on the ground would cause a collision. The cactus front arrives in 60 / 6 = 10 frames. Allowing for the cactus width and the dinosaur width, it passes completely in about (60 + 25 + 44) / 6 = 22 frames. A jump lasts roughly 36 frames, so the dinosaur can be airborne while it passes.
Side view of the gap, each dash is approximately 10 pixels: dinosaur |------| obstacle.

Example state: The dinosaur is on the ground. A cactus is 500 pixels beyond its front, moving toward it at 6 pixels per frame. Answer: run. Explanation: A jump now would finish before the cactus arrived.
Side view of the gap, each dash is approximately 10 pixels: dinosaur |--------------------------------------------------| obstacle.

Example state: The dinosaur is on the ground. A cactus is 180 pixels beyond its front, 25 pixels wide and 50 pixels tall, approaching at 6 pixels per frame. Answer: run. Explanation: Wait for this six-frame turn. Jumping now would put the descent too early, while the cactus is still passing.
Side view of the gap, each dash is approximately 10 pixels: dinosaur |------------------| obstacle.

Example state: The dinosaur is in the air with its feet 80 pixels above the ground, falling at 2 pixels per frame. A cactus is 20 pixels beyond its front, 25 pixels wide and 50 pixels tall, approaching at 6 pixels per frame. Answer: run. Explanation: Let the current jump continue over the cactus. Ducking would force the dinosaur down into it.
Side view of the gap, each dash is approximately 10 pixels: dinosaur |--| obstacle.

Compare two cases with the same grounded dinosaur, cactus size, and speed of 6 pixels per frame. At a distance of 180 pixels, choose run: the cactus arrives too late for a jump started now. At a distance of 60 pixels, choose jump: the cactus will arrive soon enough for this jump to clear it. The distance changes the answer even though both observations mention a cactus.

Example state: The dinosaur is on the ground. A cactus is 40 pixels beyond its front, approaching at 6 pixels per frame. Answer: jump. Explanation: Waiting another six frames would leave almost no clearance; begin rising now.
Side view of the gap, each dash is approximately 10 pixels: dinosaur |----| obstacle.

Example state: The dinosaur is on the ground. A cactus is 300 pixels beyond its front, approaching at 6 pixels per frame. Answer: run. Explanation: An obstacle being visible does not mean it is time to jump. It will still be far ahead after this six-frame turn.
Side view of the gap, each dash is approximately 10 pixels: dinosaur |------------------------------| obstacle.

Example state: The dinosaur is on the ground. A cactus is 120 pixels beyond its front, 25 pixels wide and 50 pixels tall, moving toward it at 6 pixels per frame. Answer: run. Explanation: Keep running for this six-frame turn. There is time to get closer before starting a jump, so it will not land too early.
Side view of the gap, each dash is approximately 10 pixels: dinosaur |------------| obstacle.

Example state: The dinosaur is on the ground. A cactus is 200 pixels beyond its front, 34 pixels wide and 35 pixels tall, moving toward it at 6 pixels per frame. Answer: run. Explanation: This shorter cactus is still too far away. Continue running for six frames and look again before jumping.
Side view of the gap, each dash is approximately 10 pixels: dinosaur |--------------------| obstacle.

State: The dinosaur is on the ground. A cactus is 120 pixels beyond its front, 25 pixels wide and 50 pixels tall, moving toward it at 6 pixels per frame. 
Side view of the gap, each dash is approximately 10 pixels: dinosaur |------------| obstacle.
